subject: Commitment landing zone — GPU sourcing playbook & MAP
messages:
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: sarah.lang@helium.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Commitment landing zone — GPU sourcing playbook & MAP

Sarah — thanks again for the time on Friday. As promised, I attached a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and a short GPU sizing reference to align procurement and engineering expectations before we move to a binding reservation. High level summary below and asks for this week.

High-level ask: lock a 3-month Dedicated pool commitment tailored for your production inference profile (low-latency chat + episodic batch embeddings). We want to make sure the MAP captures the procurement gating items so your finance/procurement team can pipeline PR and approval.

Key runbook items (draft):
- Evaluation (2 weeks): POC perf targets (p50 latency < 120ms @ 512 tokens, throughput 600 tpm) on a 4-worker A100 80GB baseline.
- Acceptance (1 week): smoke tests, latency / tail-latency verification, traffic replay.
- Capacity reservation (lead times): Dedicated reserved pool — target lock window 8–12 weeks from PO acceptance; Private/offline/on-prem option commonly adds 4–6 weeks for hardware provisioning and network validation.
- GPU pool sizing: initial booking recommendation = 12 x A100-80GB (balanced for chat + embeddings); optional H100 tranche for peak QPS (estimate +20% perf uplift, reduces unit count).
- Billing & contract milestones: draft SOW + PO, invoice schedule, and start-of-service acceptance criteria.

Immediate asks: please share the name and contact at procurement (for PR lead) and confirm if Helium prefers a Dedicated hosted pool (recommended) or Private deployment. I attached the MAP template (Helium_MAP_v1.xlsx) — fill the procurement/PO columns and I’ll turn it into a formal MRA for signatures.

Att: Helium_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP template), gpu_sizing_reference.pdf (reference table)

— Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

- Procurement: Meera Patel, meera.patel@helium.ai, +1 415-555-0134

I’ve populated the MAP procurement columns at a high level and uploaded to your Drive link; I flagged two constraints: Helium's fiscal approval cycle closes on Dec 15 and our legal will want a 30-day data residency clause clarified for Private deployments.

Quick questions: can Redwood provide an exact ETA range for delivery acceptance tests if we sign PO by Dec 1? Also, do you have an estimated pricing delta for an H100 tranche vs A100 baseline (we want a rough $/slot number for internal run-rate modeling).

— Sarah
Head of Engineering — Helium AI

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 14:22 Markus K <markus_klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Markus — thanks, this is clear and helpful. We prefer Dedicated hosted for time-to-value but want a contingency plan for Private (on-prem) if compliance gates push longer.

Sarah — hi, looping procurement + ops details. Short answers to your two asks:
1) ETA if PO by Dec 1: we can target acceptance testing start between Jan 12–Jan 26 (8–10 weeks; tighter 8-week path if PR received with immediate invoice/PO confirmation). That includes rack scheduling, image bake, and staging warm-up.
2) H100 vs A100 pricing: approximate delta = +35–45% per-slot list (H100 improves throughput for heavy attention workloads, so fewer slots needed; we'll provide modeled scenarios in the MAP).

Sizing note: if Helium wants to maintain latency SLOs plus embedding batch throughput, the minimal pragmatic pool is 8 x A100-80GB for the eval/pooled POC; production baseline we recommend 12–16 slots. If you go H100, you could target 8–10 slots for equivalent throughput.

Procurement checklist I recommend we capture in MAP (I’ll add these to the spreadsheet):
- PO + billing contact and billing address
- Procurement lead and legal review timelines
- Acceptance criteria sign-off owner (Helium eng manager)
- SOC2 evidence request timing (if required)

Attachments referenced: added a short pricing-model worksheet to the Drive link and updated Helium_MAP_v1.xlsx with an initial capacity scenario.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Commitment landing zone — GPU sourcing playbook & MAP

Sarah / Victor — thanks for the clarity and the MAP updates. We pulled legal/finance/ops into the loop and here are concrete next steps to move toward a PO lock: 

Planned mutual-action milestones (agreed draft):
1) Finalize MAP spreadsheet (by Nov 19) — Helium to confirm procurement contacts, PR cadence, and desired start window.
2) Security packet delivery (Redwood) — Redwood to send SOC2 + infra attestation and network diagram by Nov 21.
3) PO submission target (Helium) — Dec 1 (Helium internal approval window).
4) Reservation lock & invoice (Redwood) — once PO received and payment terms agreed, we create the Dedicated reservation and schedule onboarding slot. Expected acceptance testing start window: Jan 12–26 (8–10 weeks post-PO).
5) Production ramp (Helium + Redwood) — 2–4 week ramp with traffic replay and SLO verification; rollback policy: capacity reductions allowed at quarter boundaries with 30-day notice and pro-rated credit for unused full-month tranches (standard in our Dedicated contracts).

A few operational clarifications:
- Price protection: Redwood can offer a 12-month price lock on committed slots if Helium signs a 12-month reserved capacity contract. I’ll note this option in the MAP with a checkbox for contract review.
- H100 tranche: we can provide modeled scenarios and a tranche addendum; lead times are similar but final procurement depends on inventory at time of PO.
- Private/on-prem: lead times typically add 4–6 weeks for hardware procurement and network validation; we recommend Dedicated for initial go-live to reduce risk.

I attached the updated MAP (Helium_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short acceptance checklist PDF to the Drive link. If Helium is aligned, Markus will draft a short statement-of-work and I’ll coordinate finance to lock pricing.

Next call: propose Nov 19 10am PT to review final MAP and pricing scenarios — does that work for you?

— Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
